title: Zero-polynomial testing in coRP
statement: Let $E$ be a verifier model, and suppose its efficiency predicate declares the specified zero-testing verifier efficient. This verifier accepts malformed or ill-formed circuit encodings, and for a well-formed circuit accepts exactly when the circuit fails its modular zero tests. The language of encodings of nonempty, well-formed arithmetic circuits over the integers that compute the zero polynomial belongs to coRP relative to $E$: a verifier for its complement accepts with probability at least $2/3$ on every input in the complement and rejects every input in the language with certainty.
hypotheses_covered: The model $E$ regards the Boolean zero-testing verifier as efficient.
